implementationPlan.description: Implement the minimum claim composition in work-claim.ts. Exact-snapshot the outer record first, then exact-snapshot each section immediately before its existing leg, accepting only ordinary/null-prototype own-data records with the declared keys and a safe dense own-data liveClaims array; catch/reject proxies and descriptor traps without reading getters. Map structural failures to WORK_PAYLOAD_MALFORMED at the owning leg with AUTHORITY/null while retaining the established lease -> slotCeiling -> providerSlot -> budgetReservation -> effectIntent precedence and all upstream mappings. At the effect leg, distinguish a structurally valid non-'claim' kind as WORK_INTENT_COMMAND_MISMATCH, then invoke applyEffectCommand only with a server-owned {kind:'claim'} literal. Return both reservation and the exact shifted result.view from the single reserveForAdmission call, construct all five typed successors only after every leg succeeds, and rely on the existing deep-freeze boundary without freezing or aliasing caller input. Add concise contract comments only where the fixed-command or second budget output would otherwise be non-obvious; keep this source below 250 lines if practical and never approach 400.
implementationPlan.note:
Claim composition implemented; GREEN. apps/daemon/src/work/work-claim.ts is 158 -> 249 physical lines (under the <=250 target).

Two local hostile-shape helpers, both descriptor-based so a caller getter is NEVER invoked:
- `mirror(value, keys, exact)` — refuses a non-object/array, a prototype other than Object.prototype or null, any symbol or undeclared own key, a non-enumerable or accessor descriptor, and anything that throws (whole body in try/catch, so a throwing proxy trap refuses instead of propagating). `keys === null` mirrors any own string keys; `exact` additionally requires every declared key. Sections pass `exact: false` deliberately so a MISSING fact still reaches its own leg and keeps that leg's upstream code — this is what preserves the existing "slot section carries no dimension" -> upstream AUTHORITY_MALFORMED_INPUT refusal.
- `mirrorList(value)` — dense own-data array mirror. The own-key count must equal `length + 1` (indices plus `length`), which rejects a hole or a smuggled key AND bounds the loop, so a proxy reporting a colossal length cannot spin.

Composition:
- `readClaimSections` now mirrors the OUTER record exactly (all five keys required) plus the liveClaims container, and returns the four section values RAW; each section is mirrored immediately before its own leg. Outer/container faults keep the pre-existing leg "lease".
- Leg order unchanged: lease -> slotCeiling -> providerSlot -> budgetReservation -> effectIntent. Structural faults map to WORK_PAYLOAD_MALFORMED at the owning leg with AUTHORITY/upstreamCode null. All pre-existing upstream mappings kept verbatim.
- `CLAIM_EFFECT_COMMAND = Object.freeze({kind:"claim"})` is a server-owned literal; the caller's command is only INSPECTED, never forwarded. `checkClaimCommand` accepts exactly `{kind:"claim"}`; an own-data record whose `kind` is any other string is WORK_INTENT_COMMAND_MISMATCH/effectIntent/AUTHORITY/null; anything else is WORK_PAYLOAD_MALFORMED at the same leg.
- `claimBudget` returns BOTH outputs of the single `reserveForAdmission` call; the shifted view is retained verbatim, never recomputed and never re-reserved.
- `Leg<T>` is generic, so all five successors are typed at construction and built only after every leg succeeds.

Test-matrix defect the trap counter caught (worth recording): the "throwing descriptor trap" poison originally proxied a FOREIGN target `{probeKey:"value"}`; the undeclared-key check refused it first, the trap never fired, and 5 cases silently degraded into ordinary malformed records. `expect(probe.hits).toBeGreaterThan(0)` failed on exactly those 5. Fixed by proxying the REAL record.

implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial review, three mutation drills, and three commits.

REVIEW FINDING FIXED (real, found by reviewing my own diff): `checkClaimCommand` interpolated the caller's `kind` into the refusal message unbounded. A probe against the production surface confirmed a 20,000-char kind produced a 20,051-char message — a refusal that amplifies to the size of the request. Now `kind.slice(0, 32)`, with a regression test pinning the cut in BOTH directions (`toContain("X".repeat(32))` and `not.toContain("X".repeat(33))`), so widening or removing the bound reddens.

MUTATION DRILLS — each applied to production, run, then reversed by exact Edit (never git checkout/reset/stash) and confirmed SHA-256 identical.
Pre-drill: work-claim.ts fce5a249…3140, work-kernel.ts 295c951f…96e6.
A. `kind !== "claim"` -> `kind !== "arm"` in the mismatch branch. 4 named tests red, including "refuses the arm command as a command mismatch" with `expected 'WORK_PAYLOAD_MALFORMED' to be 'WORK_INTENT_COMMAND_MISMATCH'`, plus 3 catching the inverse direction (extra-key claim commands misclassified as MISMATCH). Restored: hash exact.

C. dropped `!("value" in descriptor)` from `mirror`. 7 red across the accessor and descriptor-trap-yields-accessor poisons on outer/lease/slot/budget, e.g. `expected 'AUTHORITY_MALFORMED_INPUT' to be null` and `expected 'budgetReservation' to be 'lease'` — proving the hostile matrix is live, not decorative. Restored: hash exact.

CHECKLIST WALKED. Concurrency: module is pure, no mutable module state; CLAIM_EFFECT_COMMAND is frozen and never handed downstream by reference (the runner's exactRecord copies it). TOCTOU: one descriptor read per key, value copied immediately. Error paths: no IO, handles, or partial writes. Retry: reserveForAdmission is called exactly once and is itself pure. Enormous input: the liveClaims loop is bounded by `Reflect.ownKeys().length`, so a proxy reporting a colossal length cannot spin. Injection: only the (now bounded) kind echo, a plain diagnostic string.

DISCLOSED, NOT FIXED (pre-existing upstream, out of scope): a granted result's `successors.effectIntent.leaseBinding` aliases the caller's lease record, and the RUNNER's `transitioned()` deep-freezes it. A production probe confirms `Object.isFrozen(callerLease)` flips false -> true across claimWork, while the caller's intent/view/slot objects stay unfrozen and NO value changes (both "does not mutate the caller's input" tests pass on JSON byte comparison). This predates the diff — `transitioned` already deep-froze the intent graph — and fixing it means editing packages/runner, which epic rail 2 and the task scope forbid.
